# Write Markdown

`make pptx`, `make html` and `make pdf` turn one `.qmd` into all three.

## One source, three formats {.vcenter scale="1.2"}

- `##` starts a slide, `#` a section divider like the one before this
- **Bold**, *italic*, `inline code` and [links](https://quarto.org) as usual
- `make pptx`: PowerPoint on the NCAR template, Poppins embedded
- `make html`: a revealjs deck with speaker view and a whiteboard
- `make pdf`: the NCAR beamer theme, for handouts

† A paragraph that starts with a dagger becomes a slide footnote.

::: {.notes}
Speaker notes live in a `::: {.notes}` div: the PowerPoint notes pane, the
revealjs speaker view (`s`), never on the slide itself.
:::

## The MPAS-A dynamical core {.shrink}

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\partial \mathbf{V}_H}{\partial t} &=
  -\frac{\rho_d}{\rho_m}\left[\nabla_\zeta\!\left(\frac{p}{\zeta_z}\right)
  - \frac{\partial (\mathbf{z}_H\, p)}{\partial \zeta}\right]
  - \eta\,\mathbf{k}\times\mathbf{V}_H
  - \mathbf{v}_H\,\nabla_\zeta\!\cdot\mathbf{V}
  \\ &\quad - \frac{\partial(\Omega\,\mathbf{v}_H)}{\partial\zeta}
  - \rho_d\,\nabla_\zeta K + \mathbf{F}_{V_H} \\
\frac{\partial W}{\partial t} &=
  -\frac{\rho_d}{\rho_m}\left[\frac{\partial p}{\partial\zeta} + g\,\tilde\rho_m\right]
  - \left(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{v}\,W\right)_\zeta + F_W \\
\frac{\partial \Theta_m}{\partial t} &= -\left(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{V}\,\theta_m\right)_\zeta + F_{\Theta_m} \\
\frac{\partial \tilde\rho_d}{\partial t} &= -\left(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{V}\right)_\zeta \\
\frac{\partial Q_j}{\partial t} &= -\left(\nabla\cdot\mathbf{V}\,q_j\right)_\zeta
  + \tilde\rho_d\,S_j + F_{Q_j}
\end{aligned}
$$

† Skamarock et al. (2012), *Mon. Wea. Rev.* 140, 3090–3105; curvature and mixing are in the *F*s.

::: {.notes}
Nonhydrostatic, fully compressible equations in flux form on the
terrain-following height coordinate $\zeta$. $\tilde\rho_d = \rho_d/\zeta_z$;
the prognostic fluxes are $\mathbf{V} = \tilde\rho_d\,\mathbf{v}$ (horizontal
part $\mathbf{V}_H$, vertical $W$), $\Theta_m = \tilde\rho_d\,\theta_m$ and
$Q_j = \tilde\rho_d\,q_j$. $\theta_m = \theta\,(1 + (R_v/R_d)\,q_v)$, $\eta$
is the absolute vertical vorticity, $K$ the kinetic energy, $\Omega$ the
vertical mass flux through $\zeta$ surfaces.

The math is ordinary LaTeX between `$$`: OMML equations in pptx, MathJax in
HTML, a serif math font beside Poppins in the PDF.
:::

## Code, static and live {scale="1.15"}

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#PBS -l select=4:ncpus=128:mpiprocs=128
mpiexec ./atmosphere_model
```

```{bash}
#| echo: true
awk 'BEGIN { for (p = 1; p <= 512; p *= 8)
  printf "%4d ranks: speedup %5.1f\n",
         p, 1 / (0.05 + 0.95 / p) }'
```

::: {.notes}
The first block is highlighted only. The second is a `{bash}` cell: it runs
at render time on the build host and its output is baked into every format.
The deck opts in with `engine: jupyter` and `jupyter: bash` in its front
matter.
:::

# Diagrams and layout

Diagrams are drawn at build time; photo, closing and short slides
are a class away.

## How a deck is built

::: {.notes}
A `{mermaid}` cell: a PNG in pptx and PDF, drawn live in the HTML deck in the
brand colors. `%%| fig-width` sets its size. Text after a diagram would split
the pptx slide, so the explanation lives in these notes.
:::

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 10
flowchart LR
    QMD["deck.qmd"] --> Q["quarto render"]
    Q --> P["pptx + post-processing"]
    Q --> H["revealjs HTML"]
    Q --> B["beamer PDF"]
    P --> OUT["one NCAR look"]
    H --> OUT
    B --> OUT
```

## A full-bleed photo slide {.feature background-image="images/example.jpg"}

### Photo slides

`{.feature background-image="images/example.jpg"}` on the heading fills the
slide with the photo; a `###` block puts the text on a panel.

## A short slide, centered and scaled {.center scale="1.4"}

| Target | Builds |
|---|---|
| `make pptx` | `quickstart.pptx` |
| `make html` | `quickstart.html` |
| `make pdf` | `quickstart.pdf` |
| `make qa` | all three, then checks them |

::: {.notes}
`{.center scale="1.4"}` on the heading centers the body and scales it up.
:::
